objective: Study-guide review — Study Guide — Session 2: Practical Agentic Workflow Controls: 1. Where Session 2 sits (continuity + WHY→HOW callback).

rows: "How do we let it do that SAFELY?"

blocks.text: The hinge sentence (say it aloud; put it on the bridge slide):

In Session 1 you saw an agent that can read code, write a fix, run tests, and summarize an incident. The same same capability can expose sensitive records or change state without authority when its scope is wrong. Session 2 is about the guardrail that makes the difference — not by slowing the agent down, but by making every action requested, approved, proven, and recorded.

WHY→HOW callback (C7). S1 gave the posture — four principles: read-only first · least privilege · human-approves-writes · audit-everything. S2 is the operationalization of exactly those four principles into a named, runnable control pattern. Surface the vocabulary map here, not only at S5. [SRC: design/S2_workflow_controls.md §1; §6 callback map] [SRC: COMMITTED_SCOPE.md — S1 safe-adoption topics]

Vocabulary map (print on the take-home one-pager; introduce verbally here). principle (the S1 posture) → control (a thing you put in place) → gate (a control that can stop an action) → proof / signal (evidence a control produces). The four S2 controls are the controls; the Approval Gate is the gate; Execution Proof and the Audit Trail are the signals. [SRC: design/RUN_OF_SHOW_v1.2_polished.md §0(a⁗′) vocabulary-reconciliation]
